Codecov provides highly integrated tools to group, merge, archive and compare coverage reports. Whether your team is comparing changes in a pull request or reviewing a single commit, Codecov will improve the code review workflow and quality.

## Code coverage done right.®

1. Upload coverage reports from your CI builds.
2. Codecov merges all builds and languages into one beautiful coherent report.
3. Get commit statuses, pull request comments and coverage overlay via our browser extension.

When Codecov merges your uploads it keeps track of the CI provider (inc. build details) and user specified context, e.g. `#unittest` ~ `#smoketest` or `#oldcode` ~ `#newcode`. You can track the `#unittest` coverage independently of other groups. [Learn more here](
http://docs.codecov.io/docs/flags)

Through **Codecov's Browser Extension** reports overlay directly in GitHub UI to assist in code review in [Chrome](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/codecov/gedikamndpbemklijjkncpnolildpbgo) or Firefox (https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/codecov/)

*Highly detailed* **pull request comments** and *customizable* **commit statuses** will improve your team's workflow and code coverage incrementally.

**File backed configuration** all through the `codecov.yml`. 

## FAQ
- Do you **merge multiple uploads** to the same commit? **Yes**
- Do you **support multiple languages** in the same project? **Yes**
- Can you **group coverage reports** by project and/or test type? **Yes**
- How does **pricing** work? Only paid users can view reports and post statuses/comments.

reviews.body:
Thanks, this looks right to me. The WASM and nix-js failures come from the new throwing-callback test (note inline). Otherwise I couldn't find a writer that skips `MakeUnique()`.

To check that, I made every `Halfedges` setter (`SetStart`, `SetEnd`, `SetPair`, `SetProp`, `MakeInvalid`) log whenever any of its three arrays was still shared, and ran the full suite: no hits. As a control, dropping the `MakeUnique()` in `SortGeometry` gives about a thousand hits, and your `SharedTopologyCopyIsolation` fails, so the new tests do catch that kind of slip.

Thanks, both look good to me. I checked locally that `SharedVecCopyAssignmentFromMovedFrom` hits the UBSan null-pointer error at `vec.h:153` with the old `operator=`, and passes with the new one. Folding the copy constructor into plain `*this = vec` reads nicely now that assignment covers the moved-from case.

comments.body:
Thanks, @zmerlynn. Both review points are addressed in `f7928a234891089683ea41b65a4f8b4bd0d98f43`.

- The throwing-callback test now excludes `__EMSCRIPTEN__`. I reproduced the original abort with Emscripten 5.0.2, then rebuilt with the guard: the three applicable SharedVec/topology tests pass and the throwing test is absent from the WASM test list.
- Copy assignment now handles a moved-from SharedVec's null counter before releasing the destination, using the existing empty-vector move path. The new regression covers empty, unique nonempty and shared nonempty destinations, subsequent reuse/copy/detach, and the original owner's contents. The original ASan/UBSan null-counter failure now exits cleanly (local LeakSanitizer disabled).

The six focused native tests pass with strict/debug/assert enabled, including the throwing and concurrent cases. clang-format 20.1.8 and `git diff --check` pass. [CI](https://github.com/elalish/manifold/actions/runs/44003802416) and [TSAN](https://github.com/elalish/manifold/actions/runs/44003802422) have now passed for this head: all 45 checks are successful, including WASM/nix-js, ASan/UBSan, TSAN, the performance guard and formatting. Could you take another look?

Thanks for the approval and the independent UBSan check, @zmerlynn. The reviewed head `f7928a234891089683ea41b65a4f8b4bd0d98f43` is unchanged, all 45 checks are successful (including WASM/nix-js, ASan/UBSan, TSAN and the performance guard), and GitHub reports no merge conflicts. Could a maintainer merge this when ready?
